_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for AAPL retrospectives (retro/build_aapl.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern); every Apple earnings release of the period came after the close. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), each field of the latest guide for the current fiscal year published by AS_OF, and events published since that vintage. Apple's fiscal year is the 52 or 53-week period that ends on the last Saturday of September. Values are as reported (GAAP), per share on the basis of the filing that published them; a vintage takes each year from the latest 10-K that reports it, and eps_published / shares_published give such a year's own publication date, so a stock split ('splits') restates exactly the per-share facts published before its effective date. Apple guides one quarter at a time: each release gives the next quarter's revenue (a dollar level) and diluted EPS, read as growth against the same quarter a year earlier (prior_sales_b, from that quarter's own release); no release or filing of the period gives a full-year revenue, EPS or operating-margin guide. A 10-Q's or 10-K's gross-margin expectation (gm_pct for a quarter, gm_guide_pct for a fiscal year) is shown in the guide line and feeds no input. A print's margins and growth rates are derived from the published income statement and data sheet (the raw figures are in its notes); non_mac_pct is the growth of net sales less Mac (CPU) net sales. rule_t holds the ten annual values (FY1998-FY2007) behind the engine's signal thresholds. Edit only to add newly published facts or fix a transcription error against the cited filing. A filing that re-presents a 10-K is a vintage of its own: the FY2009 10-K/A of 2010-01-26 revises FY2007-FY2009 for the accounting principles Apple adopted retrospectively in Q1 FY10, and amends Items 6-8 only, so its business wording is the FY2009 10-K's. A guide's prior_sales_b is the same quarter a year earlier on the guide's own accounting basis, from the latest filing published by the guide's date that reports it (the revised FY2009 quarters for the guides of fiscal 2010). From FY2009 a print's lt_securities_b holds the long-term marketable securities (display only); from Q1 FY10 a print has no iPhone and Apple TV deferral (deferred_iphone_b null); ipad_units_k from Q3 FY10. From the Q1 FY13 release a guide is a bulleted list: revenue and gross margin ranges, operating expenses (opex_usd_b), other income/(expense) (oie_usd_b) and a tax rate (tax_pct), all for the next quarter and display only; no EPS guide. 'dividends' holds each declared quarterly rate from the first filing that states it; 'capital_return' holds each statement of the capital return program (shown in catalyst (5)). From Q1 FY15 the data sheet gives no iPod units (ipod_units_k null). The 7-for-1 split effective 2014-06-09 restates per-share facts published before it ('splits'). From Q1 FY16 a release may carry a supplemental exhibit (non-GAAP constant-currency growth, installed-base purchases): display material, no input. Fiscal 2017 had 53 weeks (a 14th week in Q1 FY17), first stated in the Q1 FY17 10-Q; a week is noted only where a filing public by that date states it. From Q1 FY19 Apple reports net sales by category only: no unit sales and no data sheet (mac_units_k, iphone_units_k and ipad_units_k null; mac_sales_pct and iphone_sales_pct, from the release's category table against its own year-ago column, display only), and the Mac unit signal, with no published value, scores BASE. A filing that revises a quarter's guide with new numbers (the letter of 2019-01-02) is a guide of its own, each field it states replacing the earlier one. From the FY2016 10-K no store count is given (463 in the FY2015 10-K). From the Q2 FY20 release Apple gives no outlook, in numbers or in words (outlook_short null): the no-guide rules apply. A filing that says a guide field will not hold and gives no number (the update of 2020-02-17) withdraws it (q_guide.withdrawn): the field is void in every earlier guide for that quarter. The 4-for-1 split of 2020-08-31 was approved in the Q3 FY20 release; the FY2020 10-K restates FY2016-FY2020, and from the FY2021 10-K Item 6 is reserved, so a 10-K supplies the three years of its income statement. Fiscal 2023 had 53 weeks (a 14th week in Q1 FY23), first stated in the FY2022 10-K. FY24 enters the history at the company's $6.75 excluding the one-time income tax charge of the State Aid decision (GAAP $6.08, the Q4 FY24 release's reconciliation) and keeps it in later vintages. From Q1 FY24 every release came on a Thursday after the close, and from Q1 FY25 the 10-Q follows before the next open.
